questions.solution:
Integer division is used.

Iteration 1: [latex]a=6/12+1=0+1=1[/latex], then [latex]a=a+b=1+0=1[/latex].
Iteration 2: [latex]a=1/12+1=0+1=1[/latex] again, and so on.

[latex]a[/latex] is stuck at 1, so the condition [latex]a \lt 10[/latex] is always true and printf is never reached.

Answer: The program gets stuck in an infinite loop

questions.solution:
'P' = 80 = 0101 0000, 'x' = 120 = 0111 1000.

- [latex]a\,\&\,b[/latex] = 0101 0000 = 80; 80 + '*'(42) = 122 = 'z'
- [latex]a\,|\,b[/latex] = 0111 1000 = 120; 120 [latex]-[/latex] '-'(45) = 75 = 'K'
- [latex]a\oplus b[/latex] = 0010 1000 = 40; 40 + '+'(43) = 83 = 'S'

printf uses %c, so it prints characters: z K S

Answer: z K S

i = 2 stays fixed; j doubles each time.
- i/j = 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] j = 2, print (1)
- i/j = 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] j = 4, print (2)
- i/j = 0.5 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] j = 8, print (3)
- i/j = 0.25 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] j = 16, print (4)
- i/j = 0.125 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] j = 32, print (5)
- i/j = 0.0625: not [latex]\gt[/latex] 0.0625 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] stop

Answer: 5

The loop multiplies j by i and then increments i.
- If 2 [latex]\le[/latex] x [latex]\le[/latex] 9: it breaks when i = x, with j = (x [latex]-[/latex] 1)!.
- Otherwise it runs until i = 10, with j = 9!.

Answer: ((j=9!) ∧ (i≥10)) ∨ ((j=(x-1)!) ∧ (i=x))
